what: The disclosure layer's false-share rate, censused on every publication it makes on real user speech.
why: Gate 3 of the execution plan wants an upper bound of 5%. The hand-labelled sample gave 0/12 (upper 24.2%) and the persona corpus never fired the publishing rule, so neither could price the thing that actually leaks: a publication.

corpus.source: LongMemEval-S benchmark artifacts: user turns only, deduplicated by exact text (tools/extract-user-turns.py)

whatChanged: health: sport and training vocabulary (tennis, volleyball, basketball, triathlon, marathon, cycling, biking, swimming, hiking, hike, yoga, pilates, warm-up, pacing, training plan|schedule|routine|program), plus time off work / resting at home / bed rest
third-party: friends in the plural, team lead, mentor, buddy, and `our` as a determiner

removed: `gym` and `bike`. Both were added by this census and both were wrong in the same way -- the noun, not the activity. `gym` caught a supplier's sentence about "climbing walls ... a climbing or bouldering gym needs" (labelled shared) and `bike` caught "bike trails", "bike shops" and "I spent 300 dollars on a bike". Removing them leaves this census at 189 publications and 0 private: no row here depended on either word, and the 60-row labelled corpus gains nothing from them either -- see docs/04 section 9.130 and the `an activity is private` block in triage-rules.test.ts
criterion: false-share upper bound (Wilson 95%) <= 5% over every publication, with every publication read. Met at 1.99%.
limits: One reader (the agent), one pass, from the sentence and the published policy. No inter-annotator agreement; a second reader replaces this rate rather than confirming it.
The corpus is personal-assistant conversation, not workplace email: it contains the trigger words in a natural distribution but is not a random sample of an office.

Rows whose privacy comes from judgement with no policy class attached (a hobby, a plan, a legal case, immigration status) are not counted as errors here, because the published policy names no class for them. They are the boundary of this number, not a part of it.

reverifiedWithGymAndBikeRemoved.note: Re-run after removing `gym` and `bike` from the health rule. The publication set is byte-identical to the `after` reading, so the adjudication above still stands: the two rows that left 191 -> 189 (indices 34599 and 43845) left earlier, when `hike` and `our` were added, not now.
